questions.stem: All of the following statements are true regarding minimal change disease except:

options.label: A
options.text: It is the most common cause of nephrotic syndrome in children

options.label: B
options.text: Glomeruli are normal on light microscopy

options.label: C
options.text: Electron microscopy shows dense deposits along the GBM

options.label: D
options.text: Immunofluorescence study shows the absence of deposits

questions.answerText: Electron microscopy shows dense deposits along the GBM
questions.solutionHtml:
Electron microscopy shows dense deposits along the GBM
  • Electron microscopy shows no significant deposits in minimal change disease. Only effacement of the podocyte foot process is seen.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 555

questions.stem: Effacement of foot processes can be seen in:
questions.solutionHtml:
All of the above
  • Effacement of foot processes can be seen in minimal change disease, membranous nephropathy, and diabetic nephropathy.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 555
